title: Informative censoring on the two sides of an indirect comparison
question: When censoring depends on latent risk in the source and comparator trials to different degrees, does the bias cancel in the indirect RMST contrast, what does source-side IPCW achieve, and does a one-sided comparator sensitivity analysis cover the truth?
design: Shared-frailty event and censoring processes with separate dependence in the source and comparator; 24 cells crossing the two dependences, censoring prevalence and anchored or unanchored design; naive Kaplan-Meier, source-side IPCW and a comparator delta-adjusted sensitivity analysis. 1000 replicates per cell.
answer: Informative censoring cancels in an indirect RMST contrast only when the two mechanisms match. Unanchored, with differing mechanisms the bias was -2.3 to +1.4 months against a true difference of 0.62, reversing the comparison in up to 97% of analyses; equal mechanisms nearly cancelled. Anchored comparisons were protected (bias within 0.22) because both arms of each trial shared its mechanism. Adjusting only the source by inverse probability of censoring weighting helped partly where only the source was informative and broke the cancellation where both were.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: unanchored bias -2.326 to 1.416 months when mechanisms differed; -0.080 to 0.021 when equal.
Anchored: bias -0.202 to 0.219 months in all 12 scenarios.
Source-side IPCW with a proxy correlated 0.7 with latent risk: 1.42 to 0.99 months where only the source was informative; -0.08 to -0.52 where both were equally informative.
The comparator delta reproducing the truth lay outside 0.5 to 2 in up to 70% of analyses (median 2.4 with strong dependence at 50% censoring).
not_answered: No covariate shift between trials; time-constant censoring hazards; one sensitivity parameterization; one baseline proxy. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: RMST difference at 24 months, unanchored (A minus B) or anchored ((A minus C) minus (B minus C))
methods_compared: source-side inverse probability of censoring weighting
